message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals that belong to the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Their most recent common ancestor was a mammal that lived roughly 90–100 million years ago, before the split of the major Laurasiatherian lineages (Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Cetartiodactyla, Chiroptera, etc.). Thus, the common ancestor of lion and zebra is a member of the Laurasiatherian clade of placental mammals.
